# Overview

This notebook performs **end-to-end data preparation and exploratory data analysis (EDA)** for the San Diego Airbnb Market Intelligence Dashboard project.

**Single data source:** Inside Airbnb ([insideairbnb.com](https://insideairbnb.com)), San Diego. Both `listings` and `reviews` come from the same scrape, so `listing_id` joins are clean and reliable.

**Note on geography:** the `neighbourhood_group_cleansed` field is empty in the San Diego scrape (verified: 100% NULL across ~13,000 rows). All geographic analysis therefore uses `neighbourhood_cleansed` only.

**Note on forecast:** this notebook prepares `reviews_monthly.csv` as the **input** to the `auto.arima` forecast (Chart 4). The actual forecast is implemented separately — either in Tableau via Rserve or in a follow-up R script.

## Inputs and outputs

**Inputs** (place under `./data/raw/`):

- `listings.csv` — San Diego Detailed Listings
- `reviews.csv.gz` — San Diego Detailed Reviews (with `comments` text)

**Outputs** written to `./data/clean/` and `./data/eda/`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `listings_clean.csv` | Cleaned listings (USD prices, outliers removed) |
| `reviews_sampled_scored.csv` | Per-review sentiment, stratified sample |
| `sentiment_by_listing.csv` | Avg sentiment per listing — feeds Chart 6 |
| `sentiment_by_neighbourhood.csv` | Avg sentiment per neighborhood — feeds Chart 5 |
| `sentiment_by_neigh_month.csv` | Monthly sentiment by neighborhood (time view) |
| `reviews_monthly.csv` | Monthly review volume — INPUT for Chart 4 forecast |
| `neigh_opportunity.csv` | Neighborhood metrics for Chart 9 bubble chart |
| `data/eda/*.csv`, `data/eda/*.png` | EDA summary tables and plots |

# Setup

## Packages

```{r packages, eval=FALSE}
# Run once if needed:
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "lubridate", "janitor", "scales",
  "cld2",       # fast language detection
  "syuzhet"     # lexicon-based sentiment scoring
))
```

```{r load-libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(scales)
library(cld2)
library(syuzhet)

set.seed(42)  # reproducible sampling
```

## Folders

```{r folders}
dir.create("data/clean", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("data/eda",   showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Tunable parameters

> **Note:** the final sample size may be slightly above `SAMPLE_TARGET` because each neighbourhood is given a floor of `MIN_PER_NEIGH` (small areas get a guaranteed minimum so they don't disappear from the sample).

```{r params}
SAMPLE_TARGET <- 40000                    # 30-50k recommended
MIN_PER_NEIGH <- 50                       # floor per neighbourhood
PRICE_MAX     <- 10000                    # drop rows above this USD/night
DATE_MIN      <- as.Date("2019-01-01")    # analysis window start
DATE_MAX      <- as.Date("2025-09-30")    # roughly matches the scrape date
```

---

# Part 1 — Clean listings

## Read raw listings

```{r read-listings}
listings_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/listings.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>% clean_names()

cat("Raw listings rows:", nrow(listings_raw), "\n")
```

## Cleaning pipeline

The cleaning steps:

1. Parse `price` (stored as `"$1,200.00"`) to numeric.
2. Drop rows with missing, non-positive, or extreme (`> $10,000/night`) prices.
3. Standardise `host_is_superhost` and `instant_bookable` to Booleans.
4. Parse date fields.
5. Keep `review_scores_rating` missingness as `NA` (do **not** impute with 0).
6. Select only the columns we'll use downstream.
7. **Skip** `neighbourhood_group_cleansed` — empty for San Diego.

```{r clean-listings}
listings_clean <- listings_raw %>%
  # 1. Parse price -> numeric
  mutate(
    price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(str_remove_all(as.character(price), "[\\$,]"))
    )
  ) %>%
  # 2. Drop bad / extreme prices
  filter(
    !is.na(price),
    price > 0,
    price <= PRICE_MAX
  ) %>%
  # 3. Standardise Booleans
  mutate(
    host_is_superhost = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(host_is_superhost)) %in% c("t", "true", "1") ~ TRUE,
      tolower(as.character(host_is_superhost)) %in% c("f", "false", "0") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    ),
    instant_bookable = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(instant_bookable)) %in% c("t", "true", "1") ~ TRUE,
      tolower(as.character(instant_bookable)) %in% c("f", "false", "0") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    )
  ) %>%
  # 4. Parse dates
  mutate(
    host_since   = ymd(host_since),
    last_review  = ymd(last_review),
    first_review = ymd(first_review)
  ) %>%
  # 5. review_scores_rating: keep NA, don't impute
  mutate(
    review_scores_rating = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(review_scores_rating))
  ) %>%
  # 6. Select usable columns (skip `neighbourhood_group_cleansed` — empty for SD)
  select(
    listing_id    = id,
    host_id,
    neighbourhood = neighbourhood_cleansed,
    latitude, longitude,
    room_type, property_type,
    accommodates, bedrooms, beds, bathrooms_text,
    price,
    minimum_nights, maximum_nights,
    host_since, host_is_superhost, host_total_listings_count,
    instant_bookable,
    review_scores_rating, number_of_reviews,
    first_review, last_review
  )

cat("Cleaned listings rows:", nrow(listings_clean),
    " (dropped", nrow(listings_raw) - nrow(listings_clean), ")\n")
```

## Save cleaned listings

```{r save-listings}
write_csv(listings_clean, "data/clean/listings_clean.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/listings_clean.csv\n")
```

---

# Part 2 — Clean & sample reviews, score sentiment

## Read raw reviews

```{r read-reviews}
reviews_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/reviews.csv.gz",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>% clean_names()

cat("Raw reviews rows:", nrow(reviews_raw), "\n")
```

## Sanity check: do reviews match listings?

> **Why this matters:** if someone accidentally drops in a different city's `reviews.csv.gz`, every downstream join would silently fail. This check stops execution early with a clear error.

```{r join-sanity}
matched_reviews <- reviews_raw %>%
  semi_join(listings_raw %>% transmute(listing_id = id), by = "listing_id") %>%
  nrow()

cat("Reviews matching listings:", matched_reviews,
    sprintf(" (%.1f%% of raw reviews)\n",
            matched_reviews / nrow(reviews_raw) * 100))

if (matched_reviews == 0) {
  stop("ERROR: reviews.csv.gz does not match listings.csv. ",
       "Please use the San Diego detailed reviews file from the same ",
       "Inside Airbnb scrape as listings.csv.")
}
```

## Filter reviews

We drop:

- Reviews outside the analysis window (2019-2025)
- Empty or very short comments (`< 15` characters)
- Auto-generated system messages (cancellation notices etc.)
- Non-English reviews (so syuzhet's English lexicon works correctly)

Then we attach `neighbourhood` from `listings_clean` — cleaner than relying on whatever is in the reviews table.

```{r filter-reviews}
SYSTEM_PATTERNS <- regex(
  paste(
    "the host canceled",
    "this is an automated posting",
    "cancelled by the host",
    "host cancell?ed this reservation",
    sep = "|"
  ),
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

reviews_filtered <- reviews_raw %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(date)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(date), date >= DATE_MIN, date <= DATE_MAX) %>%
  filter(!is.na(comments)) %>%
  mutate(comments = str_squish(comments)) %>%
  filter(nchar(comments) >= 15) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(comments, SYSTEM_PATTERNS)) %>%
  # English-only (cld2 is fast)
  mutate(lang = cld2::detect_language(comments)) %>%
  filter(lang == "en") %>%
  select(-lang) %>%
  # Keep only reviews tied to listings we kept
  semi_join(listings_clean, by = "listing_id") %>%
  # Attach neighbourhood from listings
  left_join(
    listings_clean %>% select(listing_id, neighbourhood),
    by = "listing_id"
  )

cat("After filtering (English, in window, with neighbourhood):",
    nrow(reviews_filtered), "\n")
```

## Stratified sample by neighborhood

Proportional allocation across neighborhoods, with a per-neighborhood floor so even small areas get represented.

```{r stratified-sample}
per_neigh_counts <- reviews_filtered %>%
  count(neighbourhood, name = "available")

total_available <- sum(per_neigh_counts$available)
per_neigh_counts <- per_neigh_counts %>%
  mutate(
    proportional = round(SAMPLE_TARGET * available / total_available),
    target       = pmin(available, pmax(proportional, MIN_PER_NEIGH))
  )

reviews_sample <- reviews_filtered %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    tgt <- per_neigh_counts$target[
      per_neigh_counts$neighbourhood == .y$neighbourhood
    ]
    slice_sample(.x, n = min(nrow(.x), tgt))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Sampled reviews:", nrow(reviews_sample), "\n")
```

## Score sentiment with `syuzhet`

> ⏱️ This step takes a few minutes for ~40K reviews. Sentiment scores are positive for positive tone, negative for negative tone, roughly in the range -5 to +10.

```{r score-sentiment, cache=TRUE}
cat("Scoring sentiment with syuzhet...\n")
reviews_sample$sentiment <- get_sentiment(
  reviews_sample$comments,
  method = "syuzhet"
)

# Save slim per-review file (drop the full comments column to keep size small)
write_csv(
  reviews_sample %>%
    select(listing_id, review_id = id, date, neighbourhood, sentiment),
  "data/clean/reviews_sampled_scored.csv"
)
cat("Saved: data/clean/reviews_sampled_scored.csv\n")
```

---

# Part 3 — Pre-aggregates for Tableau

Tableau performs best when fed **small summary tables** rather than hundreds of thousands of raw reviews. We pre-aggregate at four levels.

## 3.1 Per listing (feeds Chart 6)

One row per listing, with `avg_sentiment` joined to listings on `listing_id` in Tableau to produce the listing-level price vs sentiment scatter.

```{r agg-listing}
sentiment_by_listing <- reviews_sample %>%
  group_by(listing_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reviews_scored = n(),
    avg_sentiment    = mean(sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(sentiment_by_listing, "data/clean/sentiment_by_listing.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/sentiment_by_listing.csv\n")
```

## 3.2 Per neighborhood (feeds Chart 5)

```{r agg-neigh}
sentiment_by_neigh <- reviews_sample %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reviews     = n(),
    avg_sentiment = mean(sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_sentiment = median(sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_sentiment))

write_csv(sentiment_by_neigh, "data/clean/sentiment_by_neighbourhood.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/sentiment_by_neighbourhood.csv\n")

head(sentiment_by_neigh, 10)
```

## 3.3 Per neighborhood × month (optional time view)

```{r agg-neigh-month}
sentiment_by_neigh_month <- reviews_sample %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(date, unit = "month")) %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood, year_month) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reviews     = n(),
    avg_sentiment = mean(sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(sentiment_by_neigh_month, "data/clean/sentiment_by_neigh_month.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/sentiment_by_neigh_month.csv\n")
```

## 3.4 Monthly review volume (INPUT for Chart 4 forecast)

> Uses **all filtered reviews**, not just the sampled ones — the forecast needs the true monthly volume series, not a downsample.

```{r agg-monthly}
reviews_monthly <- reviews_filtered %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(date, unit = "month")) %>%
  count(year_month, name = "review_count")

write_csv(reviews_monthly, "data/clean/reviews_monthly.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/reviews_monthly.csv (forecast INPUT)\n")
```

## 3.5 Neighborhood Opportunity table (feeds Chart 9)

One row per neighborhood, with three metrics in their **native units** — no composite score is computed. Tableau plots `x = median price`, `y = avg sentiment`, `size = supply`. The reader interprets the quadrants based on their own investor preferences.

```{r agg-opportunity}
neigh_opportunity <- listings_clean %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood) %>%
  summarise(
    supply       = n(),
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    sentiment_by_neigh %>% select(neighbourhood, avg_sentiment, n_reviews),
    by = "neighbourhood"
  ) %>%
  # Keep neighborhoods with enough data for both axes to be reliable
  filter(supply >= 20, !is.na(avg_sentiment), n_reviews >= 30)

write_csv(neigh_opportunity, "data/clean/neigh_opportunity.csv")
cat("Saved: data/clean/neigh_opportunity.csv  (Chart 9 input,",
    nrow(neigh_opportunity), "neighborhoods)\n")
```

# Part 4 — Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

This section produces summary tables and plots that directly support the **descriptive statistics** narrative in the written report.

## 4.1 Overall listing summary

```{r eda-overall}
eda_overall <- tibble(
  metric = c("n_listings", "n_neighbourhoods",
             "price_median", "price_mean", "price_p25", "price_p75",
             "price_p95", "price_max",
             "pct_superhost", "pct_entire_home"),
  value = c(
    nrow(listings_clean),
    n_distinct(listings_clean$neighbourhood),
    median(listings_clean$price, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(listings_clean$price,   na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(listings_clean$price, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(listings_clean$price, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(listings_clean$price, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(listings_clean$price,    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(listings_clean$host_is_superhost, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    mean(listings_clean$room_type == "Entire home/apt", na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )
)

write_csv(eda_overall, "data/eda/eda_overall.csv")
eda_overall
```

## 4.2 Room type breakdown

```{r eda-room}
eda_room <- listings_clean %>%
  count(room_type) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

write_csv(eda_room, "data/eda/eda_room_type.csv")
eda_room
```

## 4.3 Neighborhood-level supply and price

```{r eda-neigh}
eda_neigh <- listings_clean %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood) %>%
  summarise(
    n_listings    = n(),
    median_price  = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_superhost = mean(host_is_superhost, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    avg_rating    = mean(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_listings))

write_csv(eda_neigh, "data/eda/eda_neighbourhood.csv")
```

**Top 10 neighborhoods by supply:**

```{r eda-neigh-top-supply}
head(eda_neigh, 10)
```

**Top 10 neighborhoods by median price:**

```{r eda-neigh-top-price}
eda_neigh %>% arrange(desc(median_price)) %>% head(10)
```

## 4.4 Price premium vs city median (feeds Chart 3)

```{r eda-premium}
city_median <- median(listings_clean$price, na.rm = TRUE)

eda_premium <- listings_clean %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood) %>%
  summarise(
    n_listings   = n(),
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    city_median = city_median,
    premium_pct = (median_price - city_median) / city_median * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(premium_pct))

write_csv(eda_premium, "data/eda/eda_premium.csv")

cat("City median price: $", city_median, "\n", sep = "")
```

**Top 10 neighborhoods by price premium (% above city median):**

```{r eda-premium-top}
head(eda_premium, 10)
```

**Bottom 10 (largest discount):**

```{r eda-premium-bottom}
tail(eda_premium, 10)
```

## 4.5 Missingness check

```{r eda-missing}
eda_missing <- listings_clean %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.)) * 100)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "pct_missing") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_missing))

write_csv(eda_missing, "data/eda/eda_missing.csv")
head(eda_missing, 10)
```

## 4.6 Plots

### Price distribution (log scale)

The raw price distribution is so heavily right-skewed that a linear axis is unreadable. Log scale reveals the shape.

```{r plot-price-dist}
p_price <- ggplot(listings_clean, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#2E5496", colour = "white") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of nightly price (log scale)",
    subtitle = sprintf("n = %s listings | median $%.0f | mean $%.0f",
                       comma(nrow(listings_clean)),
                       median(listings_clean$price),
                       mean(listings_clean$price)),
    x = "Nightly price (USD, log scale)", y = "Listings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("data/eda/plot_price_distribution.png", p_price, width = 8, height = 5)
p_price
```

### Top 20 neighborhoods by median price

```{r plot-price-neigh, fig.height=7}
p_neigh <- eda_neigh %>%
  arrange(desc(median_price)) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  mutate(neighbourhood = fct_reorder(neighbourhood, median_price)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = median_price, y = neighbourhood)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2E5496") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title    = "Top 20 neighborhoods by median nightly price",
    subtitle = sprintf("City median: $%.0f", city_median),
    x = "Median price (USD)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("data/eda/plot_price_by_neighbourhood.png", p_neigh, width = 9, height = 7)
p_neigh
```

### Neighborhood price premium vs city median (preview of Chart 3)

```{r plot-premium, fig.height=9}
p_prem <- eda_premium %>%
  filter(n_listings >= 20) %>%
  arrange(desc(premium_pct)) %>%
  slice(c(1:15, (n()-14):n())) %>%
  mutate(
    neighbourhood = fct_reorder(neighbourhood, premium_pct),
    direction = ifelse(premium_pct >= 0, "premium", "discount")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = premium_pct, y = neighbourhood, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(premium = "#2E5496", discount = "#C0504D")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Neighborhood price premium / discount vs city median",
    subtitle = "Top 15 premiums and bottom 15 discounts (neighborhoods with >=20 listings)",
    x = "Premium relative to city median",
    y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("data/eda/plot_price_premium.png", p_prem, width = 9, height = 9)
p_prem
```
